sources.exact_application: Z_i is a closed oriented real four-manifold. D_i is compact and locally contractible: a sufficiently small complex-curve neighbourhood is a finite collection of normalized branch discs with their marked origins identified, and isolated points are contractible. The relative cap isomorphism H_2(Z_i,Z_i minus D_i;Z) -> H^2(D_i;Z) identifies the map from H_2(Z_i;Z) with restriction of Poincare duality. Evaluation on the fundamental class of each curve C is exactly intersection with C. Thus its kernel, modulo torsion, is the stated K_i; every class there is represented by a finite, hence compact, cycle in the complement. For the actual cover w^(m_i)=u, x=s^(N/m_i)/w, the sum of all lifts is the integral chain transfer for total degree m_i, including a disconnected covering. Holomorphic local charts preserve orientation, and each transverse intersection has exactly m_i lifts, yielding the multiplicity factor. These source maps supply Steps 2 and 4; the whole-disc horizontal transport and the resulting Psi are proved in the receiving argument.

sources.exact_application: The component minimal model in Step 10 is a complex K3 surface, so its oriented integral middle form is E8(-1)^2 plus U^3 and has negative index 19. Each actual point blowup adds the exceptional class of square -1 through the blowup map described in the Peters entry. The previously proved inequality max(b2minus-r,0)<=3 then gives r>=16+n for the chosen n-fold blowup resolution. The source is credited for the K3 lattice; the receiving boundary-rank inequality is separately proved.

sources.actual_reading: Read the title page and the displayed formula pages, the complete point-blowup paragraph on p.8, and the surface definitions on p.9. These are the current 35-page author PDF's page numbers; no older published pp.87–88 are claimed opened in this reading.
sources.exact_application: For an Enriques surface, b1=pg=0 and torsion canonical class give chi(O)=1 and c1^2=0. Noether's identity gives c2=e=12, hence b2=10; the signature formula gives -8, hence inertia (1,9). UN33 supplies q=pg=0, e=12 and K^2=0 for the receiving properly elliptic chi(O)=1 case, to which the same explicit signature calculation applies. For a point blowup pi, cohomological pullback pi^* and the exceptional divisor E give the orthogonal splitting with E^2=-1; Poincare duality carries this splitting to the homology pairing used in UN36. Iteration adds n negative directions, so the receiving negative-index bound gives r>=6+n. This reading does not replace UN33's own elliptic-fibre argument.
